note: Attacker-controlled 8-byte input is interpreted as an H3Index and vertexNum; the index value flows into cellToVertex, cellToVertexes, vertexToLatLng, and isValidVertex.
The raw H3Index from input is passed directly to vertexToLatLng without validation, allowing arbitrary reserved bits and mode bits to reach the boundary computation.
The reserved bits (attacker-controlled) are extracted as the vertex number; this value is used as the start index into the pentagon/hexagon vertex boundary computation.
For a pentagon owner, the attacker-controlled vertexNum is passed as the start parameter to _faceIjkPentToCellBoundary, which uses it to index into the vertex array and control loop iteration.

code: for (int vert = start; vert < start + length + additionalIteration; vert++)
note: The loop begins at the attacker-controlled start value; when start > 0 and length=1, the first iteration has vert == start so the edge-crossing block is skipped, but subsequent logic depends on the vertex index.

The vertex FaceIJK is adjusted for overage; if the adjustment loops (NEW_FACE), the face and coordinate fields are modified, potentially leaving some fields in an uninitialized or inconsistent state depending on the input index.

When the edge-crossing branch is taken (Class III resolution and vert > start), the intersection point is computed from vertex coordinates; if the vertex coordinates contain uninitialized values due to the overage adjustment path, the intersection result propagates uninitialized data.

The intersection point (potentially containing uninitialized values) is converted to geographic coordinates and stored in the output CellBoundary, which is then copied to the LatLng output in vertexToLatLng.

The first vertex of the computed boundary is copied to the output LatLng; if the boundary computation used uninitialized values, the output LatLng contains uninitialized data, triggering the MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value report.
